regions.name: Rectus abdominis
regions.description: Runs vertically along the front of the abdomen and flexes the trunk.

exercises.name: Reverse crunch
exercises.instructions: Lie on your back with bent knees. Curl your pelvis toward your ribs to lift the tailbone slightly, then lower with control.
exercises.cue: Use a small pelvic curl rather than swinging your legs.

exercises.name: Dead bug
exercises.instructions: Lie on your back with hips and knees bent. Slowly extend the opposite arm and leg, then return and alternate.
exercises.cue: Keep your ribs down and lower back position steady.

regions.name: Internal & external obliques
regions.description: Control trunk rotation and side bending, and help resist those motions under load.

exercises.name: Pallof press
exercises.instructions: Stand side-on to a cable with the handle at your chest. Press forward, pause, and return without turning.
exercises.cue: Keep your hips and shoulders facing forward.

exercises.name: Side plank
exercises.instructions: Support yourself on one forearm and the side of your foot. Lift your hips to form a straight line. Use bent knees to reduce difficulty.
exercises.cue: Stack the shoulder above the elbow and breathe steadily.

regions.name: Transversus abdominis
regions.description: A deep layer that contributes to abdominal pressure and trunk stability.
regions.note: The deep abdominal wall works as part of a coordinated brace.

exercises.name: Dead bug
exercises.instructions: Lie on your back with hips and knees bent. Slowly extend the opposite arm and leg, then return and alternate.
exercises.cue: Keep your ribs down and lower back position steady.

exercises.name: Pallof press
exercises.instructions: Stand side-on to a cable with the handle at your chest. Press forward, pause, and return without turning.
exercises.cue: Keep your hips and shoulders facing forward.

regions.name: Multifidus
regions.description: Short deep spinal muscles help control individual vertebral segments.

exercises.name: Bird dog
exercises.instructions: Start on hands and knees. Extend the opposite arm and leg without rotating your trunk, pause, then return and switch sides.
exercises.cue: Reach long rather than lifting high.

regions.name: Quadratus lumborum
regions.description: Connects the pelvis, lumbar spine, and lowest rib; resists side bending.

exercises.name: Suitcase carry
exercises.instructions: Carry one moderate dumbbell at your side and walk steadily without leaning. Switch hands.
exercises.cue: Keep the pelvis level and breathe throughout.

exercises.name: Side plank
exercises.instructions: Support yourself on one forearm and the side of your foot. Lift your hips to form a straight line. Use bent knees to reduce difficulty.
exercises.cue: Stack the shoulder above the elbow and breathe steadily.

regions.name: Diaphragm
regions.description: Primary breathing muscle that also contributes to coordinated trunk pressure.

exercises.name: Controlled diaphragmatic breathing
exercises.instructions: Sit or lie comfortably. Inhale gently, allowing the lower ribs to expand, then exhale without forcing the air out.
exercises.cue: Keep your shoulders relaxed. This trains breathing control, not isolated maximal strength.

regions.name: Pelvic floor
regions.description: Levator ani and coccygeus support the pelvic organs and coordinate pressure and continence.
regions.note: Use a gentle lift followed by full relaxation. Persistent pelvic symptoms need individualized assessment.

exercises.name: Gentle pelvic-floor contraction and release
exercises.instructions: While breathing normally, gently lift the muscles you would use to hold back gas. Release completely before repeating.
exercises.cue: Avoid bearing down or squeezing the glutes. Do not practise by interrupting urination.
